369466.title: Upper-bound conjecture for the d-distance p-packing domination number of trees
369466.literal:
Let $T$ be a tree of order $n$, and let $d$ and $p$ be integers satisfying

$$
3 \leq p \leq d.
$$

Here, $\gamma_d^p(T)$ denotes the $d$-distance $p$-packing domination number of $T$.

**Tree upper-bound conjecture.** If $3 \leq p \leq d$, then

$$
\gamma_d^p(T) \leq \frac{n-2\sqrt{n}+d+1}{d}.
$$

This conjecture extends the cited upper bound for $\gamma_d^1(G)$ and the paper's preceding result for trees when $p=2$. Its status is not established in the supplied source context.

375723.title: Sharp sumset lower-bound conjecture for hypercubes
375723.literal:
Let $n,m,d$ be positive integers, let $[m]:=\{0,1,\ldots,m\}$, and let $A_1,\ldots,A_n$ be finite subsets of $[m]^d$. Define

$$
p_{n,m}:=\frac{n\log(m+1)}{m\log(n+1)}.
$$

**Sharp sumset lower-bound conjecture.** The inequality

$$
|A_1+\cdots+A_n|\geq (|A_1|\cdots|A_n|)^{1/p}
$$

holds with $p=p_{n,m}$.

The conjecture asks for the sharp exponent in lower bounds for Minkowski sums of subsets of a hypercube. The paper states that it resolves this conjecture in full generality, so the conjecture is solved.

377989.title: The generic rigidity characterization by pseudo-triangulation straightening
377989.literal:
Let $G$ be a plane graph. A plane graph is **generically rigid** if its generic realizations are infinitesimally rigid, and it can be **straightened as a pseudo-triangulation** if its embedding admits a straight-line realization whose faces are pseudo-triangles. **The generic rigidity characterization.** The following conditions are equivalent:

1. $G$ is generically rigid.
2. $G$ can be straightened as a pseudo-triangulation.

This conjecture seeks a complete characterization of the plane graphs that admit pseudo-triangulation realizations. The paper establishes the result for several important subclasses, including plane Laman graphs, rigidity circuits, and certain Laman-plus-one and Laman-plus-two graphs, while leaving the general case open.

378213.title: The F–M triangle transformation conjecture for crystallographic root systems
378213.literal:
Let $W$ be the Weyl group of a crystallographic root system $\Phi$ of rank $n$, and let $F(x,y)$ and $M(x,y)$ denote respectively the $F$-triangle for $\Phi$ and the $M$-triangle for $W$, where

$$
M(x,y)=\sum_{a \leq b} \mu(a,b)x^{\operatorname{rk}(b)}y^{\operatorname{rk}(a)}.
$$

**F–M triangle transformation conjecture.** The two generating functions are related by the invertible transformation

$$
(1-y)^n F\left(\frac{x+y}{1-y},\frac{y}{1-y}\right)=M\left(-x,-\frac{y}{x}\right).
$$

This conjecture proposes a uniform relation between the face-enumerating $F$-triangle of the generalized associahedron and the interval Möbius-number $M$-triangle of the associated noncrossing partition lattice. The supplied text gives no resolution status, so the conjecture is recorded as open.

378332.title: The converse capacity conjecture for quasi-Bernoulli tree-indexed processes
378332.literal:
Let $(\Omega,S,B,\mu)$ be a tree-indexed process. Define

$$
f(n)=\mu^n\bigl(\pi_n(B)\bigr)^{-1}
$$

so that $f(n)$ is the probability that a sequence of $n$ IID picks from $\mu$ extends to some sequence in $B$. **The converse capacity conjecture.** If $P(\Gamma;B)>0$, then

$$
\overline{\operatorname{cap}}_f(\Gamma)>0.
$$

If true, this would make the capacity criterion necessary and sufficient in the quasi-Bernoulli case, complementing the Basic Theorem; the conjecture is identified in the source as the most important open problem for tree-indexed processes.

378415.title: Zigzag structure of prisms over antiprisms

$$
z=\left(\frac{8m}{\gcd(m,3)}\right)^{8\gcd(m,3)},
$$

378696.title: The Colin de Verdière parameter and algebraic shifting
378696.literal:

$$
\{k+1,k+2\}\notin \Delta(G).
$$

This would relate the Colin de Verdière parameter to the shifted graph and, via the shifted-graph characterization of colorability, imply a corresponding bound on its chromatic number. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

378720.title: Codimension conjecture for irredundant affine hyperplane coverings
378720.literal:
Let $q>2$ be a prime power, let $V$ be a vector space over $\operatorname{GF}(q)$, and suppose that $V$ is covered irredundantly by $k$ affine hyperplanes

$$
H_1+v_1,H_2+v_2,\dots,H_k+v_k.
$$

Here the $H_i$ are the corresponding linear hyperplanes.

**Codimension conjecture.** The codimension of

$$
\bigcap_i H_i
$$

is at most $k/(1+\varepsilon_q)$ for some fixed positive constant $\varepsilon_q$ depending only on $q$.

This is the self-contained formulation of the positive-density conjecture for minimal affine hyperplane coverings. The source proves it with $\varepsilon_q\geq\frac12$ for nonprime $q$, while the remaining cases are open.

378756.title: The maximal-girth dimension conjecture for l-CM simplicial complexes
378756.literal:
Let $\Delta$ be an $l$-CM simplicial complex of maximal girth. Let $c$ denote the parameter used for its dimension in the paper, and suppose that $\Delta$ is not the $r$-skeleton of the $(l+r-1)$-simplex for any $r$. **The maximal-girth dimension conjecture.** Then

$$
c \geq l-1.
$$

The conjecture asserts a lower bound on the dimension-related parameter $c$ for maximal-girth $l$-CM complexes, apart from the specified skeletons. The source gives no resolution, and the displayed assertion is also repeated in a weaker large-vertex form.

379429.title: The positivity conjecture for local Braden–MacPherson sections
379429.literal:
Let $\mathcal W$ be the Coxeter group with Bruhat order $<$ and length function $l$. For $x,y\in\mathcal W$ with $y<x$, let $B(x)^{[y]}$ denote the corresponding graded $S$-module associated with the indecomposable projective object $B(x)$. **Positivity conjecture.** The $S$-module $B(x)^{[y]}$ lives in degrees

$$
> -l(y).
$$
 One of the main problems in Kazhdan--Lusztig theory is to establish this strict lower-degree bound, which is presented in the source as a conjecture; no resolution status is supplied.

379430.title: Soergel's character conjecture for indecomposable projectives
379430.literal:
Let $\mathcal W$ be the Coxeter group, let $\mathcal H$ be its Hecke algebra, and let $B(x)$ be the indecomposable projective object associated with $x\in\mathcal W$. For a graded $S$-module $N\cong\bigoplus_i S\{k_i\}$, define its graded dimension by

$$
\operatorname{\underline{dim}}(N)=\sum_i v^{-k_i}.
$$

For $M\in\mathcal V$, define its graded character by

$$
h(M)=\sum_{y\in\mathcal W}\operatorname{\underline{dim}}(M^{[y]})v^{l(y)}\widetilde T_y\in\mathcal H.
$$
 **Soergel's character conjecture.** For any $x\in\mathcal W$,

$$
h(B(x))=C_x^\prime.
$$
 This asserts that the graded character of each indecomposable projective is the corresponding Kazhdan--Lusztig self-dual element. The source attributes the statement to Soergel and gives no resolution status.

380489.title: Linear chromatic-root bound in maxmaxflow
380489.literal:
For a loopless weighted graph $G$, let $P_G(q)$ be its chromatic polynomial, let its chromatic roots be the real or complex zeros of $P_G$, and let $\Lambda$ be its maxmaxflow.

**Maxmaxflow chromatic-root conjecture.** There exist universal constants $C(\Lambda)<\infty$ such that every chromatic root of every loopless graph of maxmaxflow $\Lambda$ lies in

$$
|q|\leq C(\Lambda).
$$

Moreover, $C(\Lambda)$ can be taken to be linear in $\Lambda$. The conjecture is the paper's principal motivation for studying maxmaxflow; the source gives no resolution.
